goal.name: Starting Strength / Mark Rippetoe

track.name: Linear Progression Program
track.description: The novice barbell program: three full-body sessions a week, weight on the bar every session, until it stops going up.

phase_sequence.name: Novice Linear Progression
phase_sequence.description: Squat 3×5 every session, press or bench 3×5 alternating, deadlift 1×5. Each session adds weight — about 5 lb on the squat and deadlift, 2.5 lb on the press. Conditioning stays minimal so recovery goes to the bar. The phase runs until a lift stalls for three consecutive sessions; that is the end of the novice period.
adaptations: Maximal strength in the main barbell lifts
phase_sequence.intensity: Heavy sets of five, every session

goal.notes: Strictly a novice-to-early-intermediate barbell methodology. Not designed for concurrent training; Rippetoe explicitly argues against mixing heavy conditioning with linear progression due to recovery interference. Scope limited to strength domains — this philosophy has no conditioning prescription beyond "don't do much." Novice completion benchmarks: squat 1.5× BW, deadlift 2× BW, press 0.75× BW.

archetype.name: Heavy/Light/Medium (HLM)
archetype.notes:
Rippetoe's Heavy/Light/Medium weekly variant. Three training sessions per week on the same movement patterns but at differentiated intensities: Heavy day (Monday) at 90%+, Light day (Wednesday) at 80%, Medium day (Friday) at 85%. This distributes stress and recovery across the week, allows continued practice of patterns at every session, and prevents the repeated-heavy-exposure fatigue of 3×5 run long-term. Particularly useful when the athlete has stalled on linear progression. The three slots below are parameterized for the Heavy day; intensity_pct_1rm values should be scaled by the day modifier at generation time:
  heavy_day_modifier: 1.00
  medium_day_modifier: 0.94
  light_day_modifier: 0.89

slots.notes: Heavy day: 3×5 at 90%+. Light day: 3×5 at 80%. Medium day: 3×5 at 85%.
Alternate press and bench across sessions. Intensity follows same H/L/M pattern.
Single top set deadlift. On Light day deadlift may be replaced with power clean 3×3.
Chin-ups or rows. Present on all three days; load does not vary with H/L/M.

deload.notes: Convert all three sessions to Light-day intensity (80%) and reduce sets to 2 per lift.

time_limited.notes: Drop accessory upper work. The three primary slots are non-negotiable for HLM integrity.

substitutions.substitute_approach: Cannot perform back squat. Substitute goblet squat or trap bar DL for lower. Floor press replaces bench.

goal.name: Horsemen GPP / SOF-Style Training

track.name: 4-Month Macro
track.description: Month by month from strength to the job: strength-dominant, then power-endurance, then job-specific, then maintenance. The strength standards are prerequisites for entering it, not its goals.

phase_sequence.name: Strength
phase_sequence.description: Month one leans on strength — four strength exposures every two weeks — with conditioning held at a level that does not interfere. RPE autoregulation sets the day's load against accumulated fatigue.

phase_sequence.name: Power Endurance
phase_sequence.description: Month two turns strength into repeatable output: barbell complexes, sandbag work and conditioning that asks for power again and again under fatigue.

phase_sequence.name: Job Specific
phase_sequence.description: Month three shapes the work to the job: rucks, loaded carries, named workouts and the PT-test events, so fitness is expressed in the forms it will be needed.

phase_sequence.name: Maintenance
phase_sequence.description: Month four holds what the macro built at a sustainable dose, with low-heart-rate recovery sessions (65% of max or less) between the hard days.

goal.notes: 4-month macro: Month 1 strength-dominant (4×strength/14 days), Month 2 power-endurance dominant, Month 3 job-specific dominant, Month 4 maintenance. Draws explicitly from Gym Jones (Twight), Mountain Athlete (Shaul), CrossFit (Glassman), and Dan John. Strength standards are prerequisites for the program, not training goals: deadlift 2.5× BW, front squat 1.5× BW, bench 1.5× BW, military press 1× BW. PT test standards: 15+ pull-ups, 200+ SSST reps (KB snatch 10min @ 53#), 3-mile run under 20:00. Sandbag get-ups, barbell complexes, and SMMF (Slow Massive Movement) challenges are signature formats. Recovery sessions are low-HR active recovery (≤65% MHR). Named workouts (Curtis P, Riley Black, Russian Aggression, SMMF) are distinct from generic archetypes.

archetype.name: Horsemen Aerobic Base (Run / Row / Ruck)
archetype.notes: Steady aerobic work. In the Horsemen macro the aerobic base is infrastructure, not the objective: it exists so power-endurance and job-specific blocks can be repeated without accumulating unrecoverable fatigue, and so the 3-mile PT-test standard holds while the strength block is running. Modality is interchangeable (run, row, bike, ruck) — pick whatever the athlete's current lower-body load can absorb. Recovery-day versions of this session are held at or below 65% MHR, which is the deload scaling below.

slots.notes: 45 min continuous at conversational pace. Nasal breathing is the pace check — if you cannot breathe through your nose, slow down. Duration scales with the athlete's session budget; intensity does not.
5 min easy walk plus hip flexor and calf work.

deload.notes: Active recovery session. Cap heart rate at 65% MHR, 25-30 min, and prefer bike or row over running so the legs unload.

time_limited.notes: Keep the main effort and cut the cool-down. Below 20 min this session is not worth doing as aerobic base — ruck to work instead.

substitutions.substitute_approach: Row or bike at the same duration and heart rate.
Run, or ruck at 20-25 kg for the same duration.

archetype.name: Loaded Carry Circuit (Farmer / Rack / Overhead)
archetype.notes: Rotating loaded carry circuit using three carry variations: farmer carry (bilateral or suitcase), rack carry (single or double KB at chest), and overhead carry (single or double KB locked out). Each variation stresses a different stability demand — farmer is grip and lat, rack is anti-rotation and thoracic, overhead is shoulder stability and core bracing under load. Distance or time per variation; circuit repeated 3–5 rounds. Gym Jones includes farmer carry and bear crawl with DBs as a loaded carry complex. Horsemen uses loaded carries as active rest between strength sets and as standalone GPP. This is durability training — moderate load, sustained tension, quality posture throughout. Not a cardio workout; not a max strength workout.

slots.notes: 5-min shoulder, wrist, and hip warm-up. Wrist circles, shoulder circles, hip hinge pattern, light KB deadlift × 10.

Farmer carry: bilateral, heaviest KB pair that maintains upright posture. Target ~75% of max farmer carry load. 40m per set (20m out, 20m back). Set down the bells, rest 30 sec, move to next carry variation. Dumbbell or barbell farmer carry if no kettlebells.

Single or double KB rack carry. Bell(s) held at shoulder in rack position. Challenges thoracic uprightness and anti-rotation. 40m per set. If only one KB available, alternate sides each round (right rack out, left rack back).

Single or double KB overhead carry, arm(s) fully locked out, scapula packed. This is a shoulder stability and overhead position trainer. Load is lighter than farmer or rack — typically 50% of farmer carry load. 40m per set. Drop to bottoms-up KB carry for enhanced shoulder stability demand at lower load.
Meta-slot: 4 complete rounds of farmer → rack → overhead carry. Rest 90 sec between rounds. Total: 480m of carrying.

deload.notes: Reduce to 2 circuit rounds. Drop farmer carry load 20%, rack and overhead load 15%.

time_limited.notes: Drop overhead carry first (highest skill demand). Run farmer + rack for 3 rounds if pressed for time.

substitutions.substitute_approach: Use dumbbells for all three carry variations. Overhead carry can use a weight plate held at arm's length. Farmer carry with barbell (suitcase deadlift position) if only barbell available.

exercise.name: Shoulder Circle
exercise.notes: Standing arm circles in both directions at varied speeds. Standard shoulder joint prep before any upper body or overhead work. Both forward and backward directions required.

archetype.name: Sandbag Complex (Horsemen GPP)
archetype.notes: Horsemen-style 5–8 movement sandbag complex performed for 3–5 rounds. No rest between movements within a round; rest 60–90 seconds between rounds. Total session time is honest GPP work — the athlete accumulates fatigue across diverse movement patterns with the same implement. Sandbag loads range 60–95 lb; select load based on the athlete's capacity for quality reps across all movements. If any movement breaks down before the round is complete, load is too heavy. Horsemen philosophy: durability and repeatable output under fatigue, not peak strength. Movements include: clean & press, front squat, bent row, deadlift, lunge, shoulder carry, get-up, half moon (arc overhead from side to side), double eagle (shoulder + squat + drag).

slots.notes: 8-min general movement warm-up: joint prep + 1 round of the complex at 60% load to learn/confirm movement patterns.

4 rounds of 5–6 movement complex. Default complex (6 movements × 6 reps each):
  1. Sandbag deadlift
  2. Sandbag clean to shoulder (alternating sides)
  3. Sandbag front squat
  4. Sandbag bent row
  5. Sandbag lunge (6 per side)
  6. Sandbag shoulder carry (20m each side)
No rest within the complex. 75-sec rest between rounds. Optional 7th–8th movement: half moon, sandbag get-up, or slasher variation. Selector populates from sandbag exercise pool based on available movements and athlete prerequisites.
10-min conditioning piece following the complex: light jog, row, or 3 rounds of AMRAP burpees. Optional; keep intensity low — this is a cool-down stressor not a max effort.

deload.notes: Reduce to 2 rounds. Drop load 20%. Maintain all movement patterns. Extend rest to 90–120 sec between rounds.

time_limited.notes: Drop the finisher. Reduce complex rounds to 3. Never reduce below 3 rounds — the GPP effect requires sustained multi-round effort.

substitutions.substitute_approach: Substitute a heavy dumbbell or kettlebell held in both hands for sandbag deadlift and row. For carry: use kettlebell farmer carry or barbell zercher hold. Load and awkward feel cannot be fully replicated.

exercise.notes: Bell held at chest level with both hands, elbows track inside knees. Gym Jones uses goblet squat (25#) in strength day warm-up: 2×5. Excellent teaching tool for squat mechanics. Low technical demand; appropriate as first-session squat pattern.

goal.name: Mark Wildman Kettlebell

track.name: General Practice
track.description: Stable swing and complementary practice modules, twice weekly each on nonconsecutive days. Progression is per successful module exposure, independent of phase names.

phase_sequence.name: Foundations
phase_sequence.description: Practice the same movements at a controllable bell. Novices use unloaded get-up positions. Do not progress through movements merely because weeks have elapsed.
phase_sequence.intensity: Clean mechanics, RPE 7 or below; rest within every minute

phase_sequence.name: Density and Volume
phase_sequence.description: Continue each module cycle without resetting it. Forecasts assume clean completion; recorded outcomes decide the next earned prescription. A higher density or volume does not authorize a heavier bell.
phase_sequence.intensity: Clean mechanics, RPE 7 or below; rest within every minute

phase_sequence.name: Repeatable Practice
phase_sequence.focus: Repeat or explicitly choose the next cycle
phase_sequence.description: Retain movement identity. Repeat at the same bell or explicitly start a new cycle after confirming technique and available equipment. Snatches and jerks require a separate proficiency decision.
phase_sequence.intensity: Clean mechanics, RPE 7 or below; rest within every minute

training_contract.notes: Repeated single-bell practice in independently progressing modules. Complete the repetitions at the start of each minute and rest for the remainder. Advance only after clean completion at RPE 7 or below. Future exposures are conditional forecasts, not earned progress. Keep the chosen bell throughout the cycle; choosing a heavier bell starts a new cycle explicitly. No snatch, jerk or double-bell progression is inferred from the calendar. Technique practice is an app adaptation.

blocks.notes: Rehearse the hinge with a controllable bell; this is preparation, not a load test.
Two-hand swings at the top of each minute; rest for its remainder. Stop if technique or breathing deteriorates.
Gentle unloaded or very light shoulder circles; omit external load if fatigued.

exercise.notes: From lying to standing with bell locked overhead throughout; reverse to return. Foundational Wildman movement — practiced in nearly every session. Wildman: move slowly through every position; there are no shortcuts.
